The phrase "all style and no substance" is a colloquial expression that can have different connotations depending on the context in which it is used. In the context of the image, where a person is giving a lecture or presentation to a group of students, the phrase might be used to suggest that the speaker is engaging in flamboyant or attention-grabbing behavior, perhaps through their appearance, gestures, or delivery, without providing substantial or meaningful content.

It could also suggest that the speaker is not well-prepared or knowledgeable about the subject matter they are discussing, and their performance is more about appearance than substance.

It's important to note that the phrase "all style and no substance" is a subjective judgment, and the interpretation of the phrase can vary depending on the observer's perspective.
